prose:
The eval asked for a fix to src/parse.ts so that parse_record returns every record of a
multi-line input. The agent first read the failing test in tests/parse.test.js, then opened
src/parse.ts and located an off-by-one loop bound in parse_record at lines 34-38: the loop
stopped one record short. The agent applied a single two-line hunk correcting the bound and
re-ran the suite; all three verifier checks pass. The trajectory review and the diff review
converge on the same defect and the same ref, so the defect is treated as one observation.
No unrelated edits appear in the patch.

The reward of 1 follows from the three verifier checks passing after the fix; the record
the case assembled supports it.

Two committed rounds with resolving refs: the tool calls show the read-before-edit
sequence, the diff shows a single hunk, the verifier shows three passing checks, and the
diff review re-read the patched range. The one corroborated claim rests on a single ref
and is counted once.
Read the failing test before touching any code.
Kept the fix to a single focused hunk in parse_record.
No regression test guards the off-by-one loop bound in parse_record.
Add a regression test to tests/parse.test.js asserting that parse_record returns records for both single-line and multi-line input.
